comment: The first territory of Oceania. Australia levies a goods and services tax,
which is a value added tax under another name: charged by the supplier,
credited to a registered buyer, declared on one form. No Union instrument
reaches it, so what this table says of it is what it says of the United
States. `vat_prefix` is null because an Australian registration is an
Australian Business Number, which carries no country prefix.
territories.name: Australia
territories.legal_reference: Directive 2006/112/EC, article 5(2): the common system of VAT applies in the territory of the Community as defined by the Treaties, and a State outside it is a third country for every rule the Directive carries. Australia levies a goods and services tax of its own under the A New Tax System (Goods and Services Tax) Act 1999, whose section 9-70 sets it at 10 % of the value of a taxable supply.
